chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ibrahim, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Beware of killing all beasts, and do not touch anything of the perfume, nor of the oil, during your Ihram. Beware of the perfume in your provisions (zad). Keep the pleasant scent upon your nose, and do not keep the foul scent, for it is not fitting that one should delight in a pleasant scent. So whoever is afflicted with something of that, upon him is its ghusl (ritual bath), and he should give charity in proportion to what he did.

key_terms.إِحْرَامُ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.زَادُ: Provisions or food supplies carried by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding perfume and scent for a pilgrim in Ihram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *al-Istibsar* details the sensory purity required during Ihram, emphasizing the avoidance of both pleasant and foul odors to maintain spiritual focus. It uniquely prescribes a ritual bath (*ghusl*) and proportional charity (*sadaqah*) for violations, reflecting the Shia juristic view that Ihram involves both physical and olfactory sanctity. The instruction to avoid foul smells while retaining pleasant ones highlights the pilgrim's state of heightened awareness and devotion.
